decisions.reason: The firm has invested heavily in this passenger data solution and promotes it publicly with a flagship government reference (UK Home Office E-borders, over 30 APIS schemes), so dropping it would write off a central, visibly committed offering.

The travel health requirements API has its own page and builds on the established aviation offer, so it keeps visible commitment; weaker post-pandemic demand can still be framed as temporary and complements the travel data portfolio, although no results are reported.

The travel and document verification platform sits close to the core offer and is still presented on its own page, so management stays committed and fits it into the integrated passenger-processing direction it has announced.
